body:
## Pull request overview

This PR addresses two ListView UX gaps: the search popover’s fixed width causing layout issues on smaller viewports, and `searchTerm` being ignored when `schema.data` provides static inline data (array or `provider: 'value'`).

**Changes:**
- Make the search popover responsive by switching from a fixed width to a viewport-relative width on small screens.
- Apply client-side filtering to static/inline data sources when `searchTerm` is set.
- Add tests covering search filtering for both inline-array and value-provider static data.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 3 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx | Adds client-side filtering for inline data and updates search popover width classes. |
| packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.test.tsx | Adds tests validating static-data filtering behavior via the search UI. |

The new PopoverContent width only switches to full-width below the `sm` breakpoint; at >=640px (including many iPad/tablet viewports) it remains `w-64`. If the reported overlap happens on tablets, consider adjusting the breakpoint (e.g., keep full-width through `md`) or using a max-width constraint so the popover adapts across tablet sizes as described in the PR title/description.

The client-side filtering for provider:'value' uses Object.values(row), which will throw if any item is null/undefined/non-object, and it also ignores schema.searchableFields (unlike the dataSource.find path that scopes $search via $searchFields). Consider guarding row before Object.values and, when searchableFields is provided, only searching those keys for parity with remote search behavior.

The client-side filtering for inline array schema.data uses Object.values(row), which will throw if any row is null/undefined/non-object, and it doesn't respect schema.searchableFields (remote search does). Consider adding a safe row guard and using searchableFields as the set of keys to match when it is configured, falling back to Object.values only when no fields are specified.
